text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:

- Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats in broad agreement with Bavarian Christian Social Union over increasing value-added tax after next elections in 1998. But two parties disagree on what the added 30 billion marks would be used for.
- Deputy parliament speaker Hans-Ulrich Klose says in report that speaker Rita Suessmuth did not use Bundeswehr aircraft for her private use, according to Der Speigel.
- Lower Saxony premier Gerhard Schroeder says VW-GM dispute over Lopez should cause lasting damage to VW chairman Ferdinand Piech.
- Coalition wants to tax life insurance, planning big cuts in conjunction with its major tax reform.
- New alliance-for-jobs talks with Kohl, employers and unions seems possible. Pressure for new round of talks grows one year after earlier round collapsed.
- Group of small VW shareholders criticise VW-GM deal, demand to know who will pay for $100 million out-of-court settlement to GM.
- CSU general secretary Bernd Protzner affirms criticism of Edmund Stoiber, Bavarian premier and CSU leader.
- German companies plan 300,000 jobs abroad, says DIHT, due to high costs of production in Germany. Most of the investment will be in eastern Europe.
- German researchers complain that massive budget cuts are leading to job losses.
- Kohl warns CDU party meeting against the spectre of SPD and Greens joining with PDS in order to take power in Bonn.
- Defence Minister Volker Ruehe rejects calls for professional army in Germany.
- German churches warn that proposed tax reform could lead to a financial catastrophe.
